dialogue.agent: Hello, how may I help you today?

dialogue.user: Hi! I’m looking for a good pair of running shoes, ideally something waterproof. My budget is between $100 and $200. Do you have any recommendations that fit those criteria?
dialogue.agent:
Here are some running shoes in your $100–$200 budget that are waterproof:

- **Columbia Men's Facet 75 Mid Outdry Hiking Shoe** – $139.99, average rating 4.7/5 (5 reviews). Features Techlite Plush cushioning, OutDry waterproof membrane, secure fit lacing, and rugged grip.

- **Salomon Men's XA PRO 3D Gore-TEX Trail Running Shoes, Black/Black/Magnet, 8.5** – $169.95, average rating 4.4/5 (318 reviews). Gore-TEX waterproofing, high durability, excellent all-weather grip, and proven performance for trail running.

- **KEEN Men's Tempo Flex Low Height Lightweight Waterproof Hiking Shoe** – $109.90, average rating 4.2/5 (49 reviews). Lightweight, moisture-wicking lining, flex points for comfort, and waterproof with eco-friendly odor control.

Are you looking for any specific features (like cushioning, style, or brand preference) or want to hear detailed features or customer feedback for any of these options?

dialogue.user: Thanks for these suggestions! I’m mainly prioritizing comfort and good waterproofing for using them as running shoes, especially in rainy weather. Out of the ones you listed, could you tell me which has the best reputation for comfort specifically? Also, which would you say is most suited for real running rather than hiking?
dialogue.agent:
For comfort and real running use:

- The **Salomon Men's XA PRO 3D Gore-TEX Trail Running Shoes, Black/Black/Magnet, 8.5** are specifically designed for trail running, not just hiking. They feature a full Gore-TEX waterproof bootie, 3D advanced chassis for foot stability, and a quick-lace system for a precise, comfortable fit. With 318 reviews and a 4.4/5 average rating, they also have strong customer approval for both comfort and running performance over various terrains.

- The **Columbia Men's Facet 75 Mid Outdry Hiking Shoe** has premium waterproofing and plush cushioning (Techlite Plush), with a focus on comfort and stability—great for mixed terrain and long wear, but it is more of a hiking boot, not specifically built as a true running shoe.

- The **KEEN Men's Tempo Flex Low Height Lightweight Waterproof Hiking Shoe** provides good flexibility and arch support with waterproofing, but it’s closer to a flexible hiking sneaker—it can handle casual running but is not as performance-oriented for running as the Salomon.

If your top priority is comfort and waterproofing for actual running in rainy weather, the Salomon Men's XA PRO 3D Gore-TEX Trail Running Shoes stand out as the best fit for both criteria. Would you like to see detailed customer reviews for the Salomon, or do you want info on another option?

top_reviews.text:
I got these for my dad. He’s a big guy, and I’m trying to get him to exercise.
We ordered him the same size he wears for all others shoes, so the size is true fit (11.5).
We went walking 2 miles this morning.
He says they’re the most comfortable shoes he’s ever worn; no feet pain, no back pain.

Day 1 Comfort!
Get them.

top_reviews.title: Longtime fan of Salomon
top_reviews.text:
I've been a fan of Salomon's shoes for a long time. As a former Special Operations Soldier, I needed shoes that could stand up to harsh field conditions while still being comfortable. I used to wear an earlier model of these shoes before switching to the Speedcross, and while I liked the Speedcross, I've come back to the Pro 3D because these shoes are more well-rounded for a wider variety of terrain and conditions. They also have a wider toe box that accommodates my need for a little more space due to two separate foot surgeries.

I am particularly fond of the GTX (Goretex) lining because it allows for a low level of waterproofing without causing my feet to overheat (read: sweat and stink), and it helps to keep the sand from permeating the shoe. When paired with Salomon trail gaiters, I rarely have any debris or sand in my shoes after long hikes, trail runs, or trailjoring with my dog.

Although I am a female, I tend to prefer the darker, more subdued colors of the men's line of shoes to the bright neon colors available in the women's line.

top_reviews.title: Awesome grip!
top_reviews.text:
Finally got to take these out today for a 5 mile run. I bought them for exactly what today’s conditions threw at me: slushy streets, icy side walks, crunchy snow covered trails, and wintry mix stuff falling from the sky.

My feet stayed dried and locked in. The laces stayed tight, and I could adjust them on the fly with gloves on. The soles gripped whatever it could, and mitigated whatever slippage occurred whenever it could not.

I bought these sneakers because I have a boot by salomon with the same sole, and I liked how well they performed.

Great shoe!

The price also fits my budget, and the rating is well above my minimum. Since everything matches my preferences, I’ll go ahead and purchase the Salomon Men's XA PRO 3D Gore-TEX Trail Running Shoes, Black/Black/Magnet, 8.5. <YES>
